extracted.intended_audience: beginners to intermediate users of the GAP system / computational group theorists learning to write GAP code
extracted.subtask_description: Tutorial guidance for writing GAP functions, using control structures and local scope, and for constructing and manipulating groups, actions, homomorphisms, and related objects in GAP. Emphasizes syntax, semantics, performance notes, and common pitfalls when using action-related functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record component access and selector syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: A component is accessible by the record name and the record component name separated by one dot as the record component selector. Example: date.year;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments to new record components are possible in the same way; the record is automatically resized to hold the new component. Records are objects that may be changed: an assignment to a record component changes the original object. See RecNames to list bound components.

rubrics_metrics.name: RecNames lists bound record components
rubrics_metrics.description: RecNames takes a record as its argument and returns a list of names of all bound components of this record as a list of strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: RecNames(date) -> [ "time", "year", "month", "day" ]. Use this to discover which components are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function definition syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: A function definition has the syntax: function( arguments ) statements end. The formal parameter list is enclosed in parentheses; there must be no semicolon behind the closing parenthesis. The function definition is terminated by the keyword end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The local statement, if present, must be the first statement of a function definition. Several parameters are separated by commas. A function is an expression and may be assigned to a variable; the terminating semicolon after a function when assigned terminates the assignment, not the function definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions are first-class expressions and assignment behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: A GAP function is an expression like an integer, a sum or a list and therefore may be assigned to a variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The value of a function assigned to a name is echoed in an abbreviated fashion (e.g., function( ) ... end). To print the complete value, use Print(sayhello, "\n"). The semicolon used after the function in an assignment terminates the assignment, not the function definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calling functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly defined function is executed by calling its name with an argument list, e.g., sayhello() for an empty argument list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the function only prints output and does not return a value, calling it will display output (e.g., hello, world.) and then a prompt on the next line if newline is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: If statement syntax and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The if statement syntax is: if condition then statements elif condition then statements else statements fi. There may be several elif parts; the elif and else parts may be omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An if statement is not an expression and therefore cannot be assigned to a variable; furthermore it does not return a value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of return in functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use return statements to return values from functions (e.g., return -1; return 0; return 1;).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about returns when functions need to produce values (examples: sign, fib). GAP may insert an extra return when printing functions to simplify execution of printed function values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recursion allowed but may be inefficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions in GAP may call themselves (recursion). For example, Fibonacci numbers can be implemented by the defining recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recursion is often straightforward to express but can be very inefficient; where possible consider non-recursive implementations for performance, since a function call is not very cheap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local variables and lexical scoping
rubrics_metrics.description: Local variables are declared with the local statement and are local to the function scope from function to end. The local statement, if present, must be the first statement of a function definition. When several local variables are declared in one local statement they are separated by commas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The usage of an identifier refers to the variable in the innermost scope with that name. Local variables prevent overwriting same-named variables in outer scopes (example: c in gcd). Formal parameters are also treated like local variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local functions
rubrics_metrics.description: You can define functions local to another function (local functions) by defining them in the enclosing function and keeping them local.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making helper functions local avoids binding them at top-level and prevents identifier collisions; alternatively they could be defined at main level but then their identifiers would be globally bound and may conflict with other uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope guarantees distinct local variables in recursion
rubrics_metrics.description: Each function call creates a new scope with fresh local variables; recursive calls do not share the caller's local variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents interference between caller and callee's loop and accumulator variables (example: np with local i and res).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test and validate function arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions that expect certain argument types or ranges should include tests for their arguments to avoid strange results when called with other arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: fib should test that n is a positive integer before proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computed information caching behavior for group objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Once information about a group (e.g., order, abelianness, derived subgroup) has been computed, it is stored in the group so it can be looked up later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a result is computed as a function of two arguments, it is not stored as attributable to a single object (example: CommutatorSubgroup(s8,s8) would not be stored). Exception: SylowSubgroup(group, p) stores the result in the group together with the prime p and can be accessed with ComputedSylowSubgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing groups and naming groups for readable output
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP prints groups by listing their generators, which can be long and hard to read; you can give a group a print-name with SetName to make output more informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SetName assigns a name that GAP will use when printing that group (e.g., SetName(elab, "<group of type 2^3>")). Note: the name does not let you refer to the group in code — identifiers, not print-names, are used to specify groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppressing or allowing output with semicolons
rubrics_metrics.description: A single semicolon after a command allows its output to be printed; double semicolons (;;) avoid printing the output of a command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginners are encouraged to type a single semicolon to study full outputs, but use double semicolons to avoid large or annoying outputs when desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing actions and homomorphisms: Action vs ActionHomomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: You can create permutation representations and homomorphisms using Action and ActionHomomorphism respectively; ActionHomomorphism can create the homomorphism directly without first creating an action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ActionHomomorphism(a8, AsList(class)) returns an action homomorphism; for efficiency the homomorphism by default maps into the full symmetric group (not necessarily surjective), but you can pass the string "surjective" as last argument to force surjectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always specify the action domain for action functions
rubrics_metrics.description: All action functions require that you specify the domain of action explicitly; they do not assume a default domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example IsPrimitive(op, [1..112]) requires the domain even if it seems obvious; omitting it can give incorrect results because the implicit domain might be different than expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default and alternate action functions (OnPoints, OnRight, OnSets, OnPairs, OnTuples)
rubrics_metrics.description: OnPoints is the default action (conjugation/powering); OnRight denotes right multiplication; OnSets, OnPairs, OnTuples describe how group elements act on sets, pairs, and tuples respectively and can be passed as optional last arguments to action functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group actions in GAP are always from the right. When acting on composite objects you must provide the appropriate action function (e.g., OnPairs for pairs), otherwise the default OnPoints may be undefined for that domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrimitive and Blocks usage to test primitivity and obtain block systems
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPrimitive(group, domain) tests whether an action is primitive; if not, Blocks(group, domain) returns a minimal block system (list of lists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blocks may accept an optional seed to request block systems containing specified points. Use the action function OnSets when operating on sets of elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PreImages for non-bijective homomorphisms and Representative to pick a coset element
rubrics_metrics.description: When a homomorphism is not a bijection, use PreImages(hom, element) to obtain the set of preimages (a coset). Representative(coset) gives a chosen representative of the coset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quotient of two representatives lies in the kernel; use Kernel(hom) to examine kernel elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action homomorphism images may default to full symmetric group for efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: When constructing an action homomorphism for performance reasons the homomorphism is defined into the full symmetric group (so it may not be surjective by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enforce that the homomorphism is onto the action image, pass the string "surjective" as an extra last argument to ActionHomomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: RepresentativeAction to find conjugating elements
rubrics_metrics.description: RepresentativeAction(a8, sgp, preim) can find a conjugating element in a8 that maps one subgroup to another (when appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to show conjugacy relationships and to compute explicit conjugating permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using < to test subgroup inclusion; use IsSubgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator < is not a subgroup inclusion test; it tests which of two groups is less in some total order and does not signify inclusion. Use IsSubgroup to test subgroup membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The equality operator = does test equality of its arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use enumerators and transversals for large sets to save memory
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP provides Enumerator and RightTransversal objects that behave like lists but compute elements on the fly and thus require far less storage than writing out all elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Enumerator(SymmetricGroup(20)) and RightTransversal(a8, norm) — use PositionCanonical instead of Position when working with transversals or special lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: PositionCanonical for special lists (transversals)
rubrics_metrics.description: For elements in special lists (such as transversals), use PositionCanonical instead of Position; PositionCanonical returns the list element representing the same object even if the exact element is not literally in the list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ordinary lists PositionCanonical behaves the same as Position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient action on cosets using RightTransversal + OnRight
rubrics_metrics.description: To represent the action on cosets efficiently, use Action(group, RightTransversal(group, subgroup), OnRight) rather than explicitly constructing all cosets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids creating and storing all coset elements and yields the action on cosets with much less memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stabilizer usage to find subgroups and index-orbit relationship
rubrics_metrics.description: Stabilizer(G, point) returns the stabilizer subgroup of G fixing a point; the index of the stabilizer equals the length of the orbit of that point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus subgroups of G can be discovered as stabilizers of points in appropriate transitive actions (e.g., action on pairs, tuples or cosets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Tuples/Orbits and appropriate action functions to build new actions
rubrics_metrics.description: To create actions on composite domains (pairs, tuples, sets) use Tuples, Orbit/Orbits and pass the matching action function (OnPairs, OnTuples, etc.) to action functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: pairs := Tuples([1..8],2); then IsTransitive(a8, pairs, OnPairs) and Orbits(a8, pairs, OnPairs) to find orbits and representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting orbits to standard domains with ActionHomomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: ActionHomomorphism can create a homomorphism whose image is a new group that acts on [1..n] in the same way that the original group acts on an orbit, allowing easier subsequent computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: h56 := ActionHomomorphism(a8, orbs[2], OnPairs); a8_56 := Image(h56); then test primitivity or compute Blocks on [1..56].

rubrics_metrics.name: Using Blocks seed to construct supergroups and use OnSets for set-action stabilizers
rubrics_metrics.description: Blocks can accept a seed (e.g., [1,3]) to request block systems containing specified points; use Stabilizer with OnSets to get stabilizers of blocks, then PreImages to lift stabilizers back to original group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When passing OnSets, ensure the second argument is actually a set (otherwise errors or wrong results may occur). Example shows how to find supergroups of a subgroup via block systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing subgroups by closure with transversal representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: You can create subgroups above a given subgroup by taking closures with representatives of transversal cosets (ClosureGroup(u336, t[43]) etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constructs subgroups corresponding to stabilizers of blocks in the induced action and can be used to build intermediate subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: OrbitLength and conjugacy class size
rubrics_metrics.description: OrbitLength(G, g) computes the length of the conjugacy class of g under conjugation; Size(ConjugacyClass(G,g)) is a probably more efficient alternative to get conjugacy class size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Size(ConjugacyClass(G,g)) when efficiency matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRegular to test regularity of an action
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRegular(G, domain, action) tests whether G acts regularly on the given domain with the given action function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: IsRegular(u336, Orbit(u336, [4,5,6], OnTuples), OnTuples) returning true indicates the action is equivalent to the right regular action of u336 on its elements.
